sheet-2.description: Sheet 2 shows the western end of Audubon's business district along the White Horse Pike, at the Oaklyn line. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned on the page so that north points to the upper left, with the Pike running across the top. It reaches from South White Horse Pike down to Oakland Avenue, and from West Nicholson Road, a diagonal road at the left edge, east to the block beyond West Merchant. East Atlantic Avenue and West Atlantic Avenue run across the sheet on either side of the Philadelphia and Reading Railway (Atlantic City Division), which is drawn as a band of tracks with a freight house on its south side and Audubon Station on the north. The upper left has frame dwellings and a row of small concrete-block garages with an auto service station and the Community Hall on large lots. Brick stores, a bank and the post office stand on the south side of West Atlantic Avenue near West Merchant, and the Logan Memorial Presbyterian Church with its chapel is at the upper right beside Wrights Alley. The lower left is industrial: the Audubon Wire Cloth Co. Inc. works, a large brick and concrete building with a machine room, the 20th Century Concrete Block Co., and the American Ice and Coal Co. with its storage silos. Dwellings with garages line the south side of the sheet along Oakland Avenue. Water mains of 4 and 6 inches and hydrants are marked throughout. The neighbouring sheets are numbered 6, 7, 3, 12 and 13 on the margins.
notes: The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch (scale bar), not 100.

West Nicholson Road, Taylor Avenue, West Merchant, East Atlantic Avenue and West Atlantic Avenue are West Nicholson Road, West Taylor Avenue, West Merchant Street, East Atlantic Avenue and West Atlantic Avenue in OpenStreetMap; East Merchant is East Merchant Street.
The railroad is labelled P. & R. Ry. (A.C. Div.); its line is the Beesleys Point Secondary in OpenStreetMap.
50 ft (scale bar; not 100 as first noted). White Horse Pike, Taylor Av, W Merchant, E and W Atlantic Av either side of the railroad, Oakland Av, W Nicholson Rd, Wrights Alley. One part.

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 shows the blocks of Audubon on both sides of the Philadelphia and Reading Railway (Atlantic City Division), between South White Horse Pike at the top and Oakland Avenue at the bottom. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper left. West Graisbury Avenue crosses the sheet from top to bottom, and Wrights Alley, a 15 foot lane, bounds the left-hand blocks; the margins name sheets 2, 7, 13 and 14 as its neighbours. The railroad runs across the middle between East Atlantic Avenue to the north and West Atlantic Avenue to the south, with no buildings on its right of way. North of the tracks the blocks are mostly open lots with scattered frame dwellings, a few small sheds, and, along the Pike, a gasoline station, a block of concrete-block stores and a large concrete-block garage with a capacity of 28 cars (heated, lighted and with concrete floor) and a row of five concrete-block garages beside it. A tin shop stands near the left side. South of the tracks, between West Atlantic Avenue and Oakland Avenue, the blocks are residential, with rows of frame dwellings with garages facing both streets, a brick building at the corner of West Graisbury and Oakland Avenue, and several concrete-block outbuildings. A fire alarm box and numerous hydrants and water pipes of 4 and 6 inches are marked, and street widths of 60 feet are noted.
notes: The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch (scale bar), not 100.
East Graisbury Avenue is lettered north of the Pike and West Graisbury Avenue south of it; both carry those names in OpenStreetMap.
Wrights Alley is shown 15 feet wide; OpenStreetMap has it as East Wright Alley and West Wright Alley.

50 ft (scale bar). White Horse Pike, W Graisbury Av (E Graisbury north of the Pike), E and W Atlantic Av, Oakland Av, Wrights Alley. One part; detected control only along West Graisbury Avenue, plus four block corners at Wrights Alley carried from sheet 2.

sheet-6.description: Sheet 6 shows the northern edge of Audubon and the adjoining part of Haddon Township north of the White Horse Pike, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper left. The Pike runs along the bottom, lettered North White Horse Pike on the left and South White Horse Pike on the right, and the line between the Borough of Oaklyn, Haddon Township and the Borough of Audubon is drawn along it. A diagonal line marked as the boundary between Haddon Township and the Borough of Audubon runs from the lower left up the middle of Cuthbert Road to the top, where North and South Hopkins Avenue follow the same line. East of it the grid of Audubon is built up with frame dwellings and garages on the blocks between East Merchant and East Nicholson Road, divided by paired North and South streets: Hood, Barrett, Davis, Haviland, Logan and Le Cato. Near the right edge an abandoned railroad and its cut cross the blocks diagonally, with a foot bridge, and several streets there are marked not opened. West of Cuthbert Road, in Haddon Township, there is a small residential cluster along Kraft Avenue, Johnson Avenue and East Cedar Avenue, including Bettlewood School No. 6, and a block of Nicholson Place near the Pike. At the bottom left stand the Colonial Village Apartments and the Cedar Court Apartments, brick buildings in courts, with a cinder block works and a lumber bin beside them. The upper left of the sheet is open land inside Haddon Township, with a few scattered buildings.
notes: Cuthbert Road is Cuthbert Boulevard in OpenStreetMap; East Merchant is East Merchant Street; Kraft Avenue is East Kraft Avenue; North and South Le Cato Avenue are North Lecato Avenue and South Lecato Avenue; North and South Logan Avenue are both Logan Avenue.
North and South Hopkins Avenue lie along the township boundary and were not used as control.
The abandoned railroad and its cut, with the streets marked not opened beside it, do not appear as streets today.

100 ft. North of the Pike, Haddon Township and Audubon: E Nicholson Rd, E Merchant, Cuthbert Rd (on the township line, Cuthbert Boulevard today), N and S Hood, Barrett, Davis, Haviland, Logan, Le Cato, Kraft, Johnson, E Cedar Av, Nicholson Pl; abandoned railroad cut at right. One part.

sheet-7.description: Sheet 7 covers the residential grid of Audubon north of the White Horse Pike, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper left. South White Horse Pike runs along the bottom, East Merchant forms the left side and East Pine the right, with East Graisbury Avenue dividing the sheet into a narrow western and a broad eastern half. Cross streets, each 60 feet wide, rise from the Pike in order: South Le Cato Avenue, South Logan Avenue, South Haviland Avenue, South Davis Avenue, South Barrett Avenue and South Hood Avenue. A diagonal line at the top is the boundary between Haddon Township and the Borough of Audubon, with South Hopkins Avenue running along it. Most of the sheet is built up with frame dwellings, mainly detached houses with garages and a few concrete-block outbuildings, standing on regular lots of 40 to 50 feet. The Audubon Public School No. 3, a brick building with a hose house, stands between Haviland and Logan, east of East Graisbury Avenue. A fire alarm box stands at East Graisbury and Logan. In the upper left a diagonal strip is marked as an abandoned railroad and a railroad cut crossing blocks and streets that are marked not opened; the blocks there are mostly vacant, with a greenhouse, a few dwellings and poultry houses. Water mains of 4 and 6 inches with hydrants run in the streets. The margins name sheets 2, 3, 6, 8 and 14 as neighbours.
notes: East Merchant is East Merchant Street, East Pine is East Pine Street and South Le Cato Avenue is South Lecato Avenue in OpenStreetMap; South Logan Avenue is Logan Avenue.
South Hopkins Avenue is Hopkins Road in OpenStreetMap and was not used as control.
The abandoned railroad and cut at the upper left are not drawn as streets and were not used as control.
The junction of East Merchant and South Haviland Avenue was rejected at 12 m by the fit.

100 ft. North of the Pike: E Merchant, E Graisbury Av, E Pine, S Le Cato, Logan, Haviland, Davis, Barrett, Hood, S Hopkins along the township line, abandoned railroad at upper left. One part. East Merchant / South Haviland rejected (12 m).

sheet-8.description: Sheet 8 shows the northeastern part of Audubon, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. It lies north of the South White Horse Pike, which forms the bottom edge, and extends north to South Hopkins Avenue, where a dash-dot line marks the boundary between Haddon Township and the Borough of Audubon. The turned north arrow at the upper left points to the upper left of the page. The ground is almost entirely residential: long, regular blocks of frame dwellings with garages at the rear, set along East Pine, Lafayette Road, Yale Road, Cornell Road, Carlisle Road and Princeton Road, which run up the sheet, and crossed by Amherst Road and Wesleyan Road. Dwelling lots are narrow and deep, most of the houses are stuccoed or frame with porches, and water mains of 4 and 6 inches are marked in the streets, with fire hydrants and a fire alarm box near the Pike. At the foot of East Pine, next to the Pike, stand a row of four brick stores with the numbers 301 to 307, a hall, and the Holy Trinity Lutheran Church, a brick building heated by steam and lit by electricity, shown in blue. Streets running in from the left margin (South Barrett, South Davis, South Haviland, South Logan and South Le Cato Avenues) end at East Pine. The blocks at the left belong to sheet 7 and those at the right to sheet 9, and are left blank. The bottom margin carries the scale bar, the sheet numbers 14 and 15 of the adjoining sheets, and a library stamp at the lower right.
notes: East Pine, Lafayette, Yale, Cornell, Carlisle and Princeton Roads, and Amherst and Wesleyan Roads, keep their names in OpenStreetMap (East Pine Street, Lafayette Road, Yale Road, Cornell Road, Carlisle Road, Princeton Road, Amherst Road, Wesleyan Road); South Hopkins Avenue is Hopkins Road and South White Horse Pike is White Horse Pike.
Cornell Road north of Amherst Road is lettered East Vassar Road to the south, offset slightly across Amherst Road.
South Barrett, Davis, Haviland, Logan and Le Cato Avenues are drawn only as stubs at the left edge and were not used for control.
Irwin Av. at the lower right is Ervin Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
100 ft. North of the Pike, east: E Pine, Lafayette, Yale, Cornell, Carlisle, Princeton Rds, Amherst, Wesleyan, E Vassar, S Hopkins Av. One part.

sheet-9-1.description: The main part of sheet 9 covers the north-eastern corner of Audubon, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north towards the upper left. It reaches from South Hopkins Avenue, the line between Haddon Township and the Borough of Audubon, at the top left, down to South White Horse Pike at the bottom, and from Princeton Road east to East Kings Highway, which is the boundary with the Borough of Haddon Heights; the Haddon Heights side is left blank apart from the ends of 1st, 2nd, 3rd and 4th Avenues. Between Princeton Road and Kings Highway the streets are laid out irregularly: Park Place loops north from Bringhurst Avenue to Prospect Avenue, and Crystal Lake Avenue and Paris Avenue run diagonally through the blocks. The northern half is a newly built suburb of frame dwellings, many lots still empty, with a few brick-veneered and concrete-block houses and some large lots facing Kings Highway. South of Amherst Road, between Princeton and Harvard Roads, are further rows of frame houses. The corner of the White Horse Pike and Kings Highway holds the sheet's commercial buildings: the New Century Theatre (movies), a row of concrete-block and brick stores along Kings Highway, a concrete-block garage and a gasoline station. Street widths of 50 to 70 feet, water pipes and hydrants are marked. A heavy line cuts off the lower right corner for the inset of South Hopkins Avenue at Kings Highway.
notes: Bringhurst Av. is Bringhurst Road today; S. Hopkins Av. is Hopkins Road; E. and W. Kings Highway are Kings Highway.
Irwin Av. at the lower left margin is Ervin Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
New Century Theatre (movies) at the White Horse Pike and Kings Highway.
Prospect Av. was left out as control: its three junctions all sat 2.8 to 4.5 m off a fit to the other streets, so the modern Prospect Avenue is taken to be off its 1930 line.

100 ft. North-east corner: Princeton Rd, Park Pl, Prospect Av, Crystal Lake Av, Paris Av, Bringhurst Av, Amherst Rd, Harvard Rd, E Kings Highway at the Haddon Heights line. Two parts: main map, and an inset at lower right (S Hopkins Av, Prospect Av, Crystal Lake Av, E Kings Highway, Lippincott) drawn at another angle. Prospect Avenue left out of part 1 (junctions 2.8 to 4.5 m off; RMSE 1.97 to 1.28 m without it).

sheet-9-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 9 is an inset in the lower right corner, set off by a heavy line, showing the ground just beyond the north-east edge of the main map: South Hopkins Avenue between Crystal Lake Avenue and East Kings Highway. It is drawn at the same scale (100 feet to an inch) and the same orientation as the main part. South Hopkins Avenue runs diagonally across the inset with the line between Haddon Township and the Borough of Audubon along its centre; the blocks south of it, numbered 217 and 218, are divided into narrow lots running back from Crystal Lake Avenue and Prospect Avenue, nearly all still empty. East Kings Highway forms the right edge, with the line between the Borough of Audubon and the Borough of Haddon Heights along it and Lippincott meeting it from the Haddon Heights side. Only a few buildings are drawn: a brick building near the corner of Hopkins Avenue and Kings Highway and a small group at the bottom edge. Water pipes and hydrants are marked along Hopkins Avenue and Kings Highway.
notes: S. Hopkins Av. is Hopkins Road today and E. Kings Highway is Kings Highway; Lippincott is Lippincott Avenue.
Kings Highway / Lippincott Avenue was hand-picked; the other three control points are detected junctions on Hopkins Road.

100 ft. North-east corner: Princeton Rd, Park Pl, Prospect Av, Crystal Lake Av, Paris Av, Bringhurst Av, Amherst Rd, Harvard Rd, E Kings Highway at the Haddon Heights line. Two parts: main map, and an inset at lower right (S Hopkins Av, Prospect Av, Crystal Lake Av, E Kings Highway, Lippincott) drawn at another angle. Prospect Avenue left out of part 1 (junctions 2.8 to 4.5 m off; RMSE 1.97 to 1.28 m without it).

sheet-12.description: Sheet 12 covers the eastern half of the borough of Oaklyn and a strip of Audubon along its western edge, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned on the page so that north points to the upper left. The North White Horse Pike runs across the top, with the boundary between Haddon Township and the Borough of Oaklyn along it; West Nicholson Road runs down the right-hand side on the Audubon side of the borough line. Between them the Philadelphia and Reading Railway (Atlantic City Division) crosses the sheet diagonally, with Newton Avenue drawn on both sides of the tracks. North of the railroad lie the blocks along West Holly, West Park and West Cedar Avenues and Capitol, with houses on most lots and, along the Pike, rows of stores and dwellings, two large public garages and an auto service station. South of the railroad the blocks between West Holly Avenue, Congress and Sylvan Avenue are lined with frame dwellings; further south the blocks along West Oakland and Walnut Avenues are platted but almost empty, and Walnut Avenue is marked not opened. A sewage disposal plant stands at the foot of West Cedar Avenue on Peters Creek, which crosses the lower part of the sheet. The abandoned railroad cut and right of way, followed by the borough line between Oaklyn and Audubon, runs from the Pike towards the creek. Along West Nicholson Road are the Atlantic Ice Manufacturing Company ice storage house, a garage and the Garden State Laundry, with the ends of Oakland, Beloit, Creston, Wyoming, Oswego and Central Avenues leading east into Audubon.
notes: Sylvan Av. is Kendall Boulevard today.
Newton Av. north of the railroad is Newton Avenue today; Newton Av. south of the railroad is Manor Avenue.
Capitol and Congress are Capitol Avenue and Congress Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
The railroad is labelled P. & R. Ry. (A.C. Div'n); its line is the Beesleys Point Secondary in OpenStreetMap.
The Oaklyn blocks are drawn about 8 degrees from the Audubon sheets (fitted rotation -58 against about -50 degrees), following the Oaklyn street grid.
West Oakland and Walnut Avenues in the lower left were not used as control: their modern lines do not follow the drawn ones closely.
Newton Av. and Manor Avenue at West Cedar Avenue, and Congress at Manor Avenue, were rejected by the fit (6 to 7 m).

100 ft. Oaklyn east half: N White Horse Pike, W Holly, W Park, W Cedar, Capitol, Congress, Newton Av either side of the railroad (south one is Manor Avenue today), Sylvan Av (Kendall Boulevard), W Oakland, Walnut, W Nicholson Rd, abandoned railroad cut, Peters Creek. One part; drawn at about -58 degrees against -50 for the Audubon sheets.

sheet-13.description: Sheet 13 covers the western part of Audubon south of the Oakland Avenue line, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. West Nicholson Road, beside the Oaklyn sheet to the west, runs down the left edge, and the streets turn slightly across the sheet, so that the western blocks along Beloit, Creston, Wyoming, Oswego and Central Avenues are drawn at a different angle from the eastern ones along Virginia Avenue, Maple Avenue and West Graisbury Avenue. West Merchant, bending down the middle of the sheet, is the main street of the western district, and Audubon Avenue runs diagonally across the eastern half. Cedarcroft Avenue closes the sheet along the bottom. The district is residential, with frame and stucco dwellings and garages in long rows, the densest rows being on Central Avenue. Along Oakland Avenue at the top stand the Audubon Volunteer Fire Company No. 1 building, a bake shop, a large building drawn in blue, and the Audubon Free Library near West Graisbury Avenue. An auto repair shop with a concrete block garage stands on Wyoming Avenue near Merchant, and a second auto garage on Central Avenue near West Nicholson Road. Water mains of 4 and 6 inches, fire hydrants and fire alarm boxes are marked throughout, with street widths of 30 to 60 feet. The compass at the lower left points to the upper left, and the scale bar, a copyright note of 1931 and the sheet number are at the foot. The neighbouring sheets are numbered 2, 3, 12, 14, 17 and 18 at the margins.
notes: West Merchant is West Merchant Street in OpenStreetMap.
Cedarcroft Avenue jogs where it meets West Graisbury Avenue; both modern nodes are on the sheet, about 56 m apart.
Printed 1931 copyright date at the foot of a sheet dated August 1930.
100 ft. Western Audubon: W Nicholson Rd to W Graisbury, Beloit, Creston, Wyoming, Oswego, Central, W Merchant, Audubon Av, Maple, Cedarcroft. One part.

sheet-14.description: Sheet 14 covers the centre of Audubon south of the White Horse Pike, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned on the page so that the Pike runs across the top and north points to the upper left. It reaches from South White Horse Pike down to Wyoming Avenue and from West Graisbury Avenue east to Walnut. The Philadelphia and Reading Railway (Atlantic City Division) crosses the sheet between East and West Atlantic Avenue, with the small Orston station at its eastern end near Chestnut. The block between the Pike and East Atlantic Avenue east of Pine holds the town's commercial core: a row of brick stores and a moving picture theatre facing East Atlantic Avenue, with concrete-block garages behind, and a golf course marked at the corner of the Pike and Pine. The Audubon Public School stands on Oakland Avenue near Oak, and the Suburban Dairies milk depot, a brick building with a concrete-block extension, is on the south side of Oakland Avenue. A cluster of concrete-block buildings stands on West Atlantic Avenue at Pine. The rest of the sheet is residential: regular blocks of frame dwellings with garages along Virginia, 3rd, 4th, Mansion and Oak Avenues, a few with brick or stone veneer. Street widths of 50 to 60 feet and water mains with fire hydrants are marked throughout. Blocks along the margins belong to sheets 7, 8, 13, 15 and 18 and are left blank.
notes: W. Oak Av. is Oak Street today; W. Pine, E. Pine, Chestnut and Walnut are West Pine Street, Chestnut Street and Walnut Street in OpenStreetMap.
The railroad is labelled P. & R. Ry. (A.C. Div'n); its line is the Beesleys Point Secondary in OpenStreetMap.
Orston station stands at the east end of the railroad on this sheet.
100 ft. Pilot sheet. S White Horse Pike to Wyoming Av, Graisbury to Walnut (Pine, Oak, Chestnut, Mansion; E and W Atlantic Av either side of the railroad, Orston station). One part.

sheet-15.description: Sheet 15 covers the eastern edge of Audubon, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, from South White Horse Pike at the top to Wyoming Avenue at the bottom and from Walnut Street on the left to the diagonal line of West Kings Highway on the right, which is also the boundary between the Borough of Audubon and the Borough of Haddon Heights. The Philadelphia and Reading Railway (Atlantic City Division) crosses the middle of the sheet as a wide bundle of tracks, with a coal bins building beside it, and East Atlantic Avenue and West Atlantic Avenue run on either side of it. North of the railroad, along the Pike and Willitts Avenue, are frame dwellings in rows, a coal yard with a large shed on Willitts Avenue, and at the upper right a large garage for 75 cars, heated by steam and lit by electricity. South of the railroad the blocks are residential, with frame dwellings and garages along Walnut Street, Spruce Street and 3rd Avenue, and a plumbers works, tin shop and several auto buildings on the blocks west of Cherry. Washington Terrace and West Kings Highway run diagonally across the lower right, and the blocks between them follow their angle, so the dwellings there are laid out on a different rotation from those at the left. The right margin beyond the Haddon Heights line is blank, and the cross streets 7th, 8th and 9th Avenue are marked only as stubs there. The compass at the right points to the upper left. Blocks along the top belong to sheets 8 and 9.
notes: Irwin Avenue is Ervin Avenue in OpenStreetMap; West Kings Highway is Kings Highway; Cherry, Walnut and Spruce are Cherry Street, Walnut Street and Spruce Street.
The railroad is labelled P. & R. Ry. (A.C. Div'n) and is the Beesleys Point Secondary in OpenStreetMap.

East Atlantic Avenue lies beside the railroad right of way; its junctions with West Vassar Road and Irwin Avenue were excluded from the fit because the detector measured them against the railroad rather than the street edge.
Chestnut Street lies just off the left edge of the sheet and was not used for control.

100 ft. S White Horse Pike to Wyoming Av, Walnut to W Kings Highway (Haddon Heights line); railroad with E and W Atlantic Av. One part. East Atlantic Avenue junctions beside the railroad excluded (2 to 4 m off).

sheet-17-1.description: The main part of sheet 17 covers the southern edge of Audubon at 100 feet to an inch, turned so that north points to the upper left. It is L-shaped: across the top it runs from West Nicholson Road past Payson and Ward Avenues and West Merchant to Cedarcroft Avenue, Audubon Avenue and Maple Avenue, and down the right side it follows the blocks between Maple Avenue and West Graisbury Avenue south through Edgewood and Hampshire Avenues to East Lake Road on the shore of Haddon Lake. The upper left holds closely built rows of frame dwellings with garages on Payson Avenue and Cedarcroft Avenue, a few in concrete block. West of West Merchant a large open tract (block 318) is crossed only by Ward Avenue, with a group of frame barns and a water tank standing in it; block 63 east of Merchant is also open. Between Audubon Avenue, Maple Avenue and West Graisbury Avenue are newer rows of frame dwellings on narrow lots. The blocks south of Edgewood Avenue and along Maple Avenue towards the lake are thinly built. The rest of the lower left quarter is cut off by a heavy line for the inset of Hampshire Avenue and East Lake Road. Street widths of 50 and 60 feet, water pipes and hydrants are marked.
notes: W. Merchant is West Merchant Street today; E. Lake Rd. is East Lake Drive.
Cedarcroft Av. jogs at West Graisbury Avenue; both corners are control points.
The modern grid has since been extended through the open blocks 318 and 63 (Tweed Avenue, Audubon Avenue south of Edgewood); those junctions were left out.

100 ft. South: W Nicholson Rd, Payson, Ward, W Merchant, Cedarcroft, Audubon Av, Maple Av, W Graisbury, Edgewood, Hampshire, E Lake Rd. Two parts: main map (L-shaped, top and right) and an inset at lower left (W Graisbury, Mansion, W Oak, Hampshire, E Lake Rd, Washington Ter, Haddon Lake).

sheet-17-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 17 is an inset in the lower left quarter, set off by a heavy line, showing the blocks east of West Graisbury Avenue between Hampshire Avenue and East Lake Road, on the north shore of Haddon Lake. It is drawn at 100 feet to an inch in the same orientation as the main part, and continues the south end of the blocks on sheet 18. West Graisbury Avenue, Mansion Avenue and West Oak Avenue run down to East Lake Road, which follows the curving shore. Hampshire Avenue crosses the inset; east of West Oak Avenue it is marked not opened and bends south-east to meet Washington Terrace, with Walnut ending above it near the heavy line. Building is light: a row of frame dwellings along Hampshire Avenue between West Graisbury and Mansion Avenues and further east to West Oak, a few on West Graisbury Avenue, and a club house in block 147. Blocks 254 and 255 are laid out in lots but empty. Haddon Lake is drawn in light blue along the bottom of the inset.
notes: W. Oak Av. is Oak Street today; E. Lake Rd. is East Lake Drive; Walnut is Walnut Street.
Hampshire Avenue east of West Oak Avenue is marked not opened.

sheet-18.description: Sheet 18 covers the southern edge of the built-up part of Audubon, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. It reaches from Wyoming Avenue at the top to Hampshire Avenue at the bottom, and from West Graisbury Avenue at the left to Walnut at the right. The upper half is residential, with regular blocks of frame dwellings and garages along Mansion Avenue, West Oak Avenue, West Pine, Chestnut and Walnut, crossed by Cedarcroft Avenue and Edgewood Avenue. The Audubon Public School, a brick building heated by steam and lit by electricity, stands at the top between Mansion Avenue and West Oak Avenue, and a Christian and Missionary Alliance church is on the Chestnut block at the right. Below Edgewood Avenue the sheet is largely open: the Audubon High School, a fireproof building of 1925 with auditorium, cafeteria, gymnasium and shops, stands beside an athletic field, and a long diagonal street labelled Walnut, with lines for water pipe, crosses the lower right corner at an angle to the grid. Rows of new dwellings fill the lower left along West Graisbury Avenue and Hampshire Avenue, while the ground between them is blank apart from a few scattered houses and a shed, and streets such as West Oak Avenue and West Pine are marked as open or not built there. Water mains, hydrants and street widths of 50 to 60 feet are marked. Cedarcroft Avenue jogs where it crosses Mansion Avenue and again at West Graisbury Avenue. Neighbouring sheets are numbered 13, 14, 17 and 19 at the margins, and the scale bar is at the bottom right.
notes: West Oak Avenue is Oak Street today; West Pine, Chestnut and Walnut are West Pine Street, Chestnut Street and Walnut Street in OpenStreetMap.
Cedarcroft Avenue is drawn with a jog at Mansion Avenue and at West Graisbury Avenue; both modern nodes of each jog are on the sheet.
Wyoming Avenue junctions along the top edge (Oak Street, Mansion Avenue) were rejected by the fit at 11 to 14 m and are left out.
Audubon High School is labelled as built in 1925; the sheet is dated August 1930.
The diagonal street labelled Walnut in the lower right is not the north-south Walnut Street of the upper sheet and carries no control.
Open ground in the lower half of the sheet has few street junctions.
100 ft. Wyoming Av to Hampshire Av, W Graisbury to Walnut; Audubon High School, open ground. One part. Oak and Mansion / Wyoming at the top edge rejected (11 to 14 m).

sheet-19-1.description: The main part of sheet 19 covers the south-eastern corner of Audubon at 100 feet to an inch, turned so that north points to the upper left. It reaches from Wyoming Avenue at the top down past Elm, Cedarcroft and Edgewood Avenues, and from Walnut at the left edge east to West Kings Highway, along whose centre runs the line between the Borough of Audubon and the Borough of Haddon Heights; the Haddon Heights side is blank apart from the ends of 10th and 11th Avenues. Washington Terrace runs diagonally from Wyoming Avenue to Edgewood Avenue and beyond, and the short, angled Sutvan's Lane links Walnut to Washington Terrace above Edgewood. The blocks between Wyoming and Cedarcroft are filled with frame dwellings and garages, a few brick-veneered, with deep lots running back from Kings Highway. South of Cedarcroft the dwellings thin out, and below Edgewood Avenue the land is laid out in long lots, mostly empty; at the corner of Walnut and Kings Highway stand the frame and concrete-block buildings of an artificial plant manufacturer with a gasoline station. The lower right of the sheet is cut off by a heavy line for the inset of the blocks between Edgewood Avenue, Hampshire Avenue and Kings Highway. Street widths of 30 to 60 feet, water pipes and hydrants are marked.
notes: W. Kings Highway is Kings Highway today; Walnut and Spruce are Walnut Street and Spruce Street; Sutvan's Lane is Sutvans Lane.
10th Avenue / Kings Highway was rejected by the fit (about 15 m off); the modern 10th Avenue does not meet Kings Highway where the sheet draws it.

100 ft. South-east: Wyoming, Elm, Cedarcroft, Edgewood Av, Walnut, Spruce, Washington Ter, Sutvans Lane, W Kings Highway at the Haddon Heights line. Two parts: main map (left) and an inset at lower right drawn at another angle (Edgewood Av to Hampshire Av, Walnut, Washington Ter, W Kings Highway).

sheet-19-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 19 is an inset in the lower right, set off by a heavy line, showing the blocks south of Edgewood Avenue between Walnut and West Kings Highway down to Hampshire Avenue. It is drawn at 100 feet to an inch in the same orientation as the main part, so that Edgewood Avenue runs across the top with the stubs of Chestnut, Walnut and Washington Terrace coming down from sheet 18, while south of Edgewood Walnut and Washington Terrace bend and run diagonally down to the left, parallel to West Kings Highway along the lower right edge. Hampshire Avenue closes the inset at the lower left. The two long blocks, 252 and 253, are divided into narrow lots running back from Walnut, Washington Terrace and Kings Highway; most are empty, with scattered frame dwellings and garages and a brick building near Edgewood Avenue. The line between the Borough of Audubon and the Borough of Haddon Heights is marked along West Kings Highway.
notes: W. Kings Highway is Kings Highway today; Walnut and Chestnut are Walnut Street and Chestnut Street.
Five detected junctions; Edgewood Avenue / Washington Terrace carries the largest residual (about 3.7 m).
